'''Michael Louis Golic Sr.''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|ɡ|oʊ|l|ᵻ|k}}; born December 12, 1962<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/G/GoliMi20.htm|title = Mike Golic Stats|website = [[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref>) is an American television host and former professional [[American football|football]] player. He played as [[defensive lineman]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). Golic is well known for his 25-year association with [[ESPN]], most notably co-hosting [[ESPN Radio]]'s ''[[Mike & Mike]]'' from 2000 to 2017. He currently co-hosts a talk show with his son, [[Mike Golic Jr.]], on [[FanDuel Sports Network]].

Golic joined ESPN in 1995 as a reporter/analyst for ''[[Sunday NFL Countdown]]''. He was an original analyst for ''NFL 2Night'' (now known as ''[[NFL Live]]''), the five-night-per-week news and information program on ESPN2. Golic also served as analyst for [[Arena Football League on ESPN]]. In 1997, Golic began serving as college football analyst for ESPN and [[ESPN on ABC|ABC Sports]], a role he continued until 2004 and resumed in 2020.<ref>{{cite web|author=Dustin Schutte |url=https://saturdaytradition.com/big-ten-football/report-mike-golic-to-stick-with-espn-in-new-role/ |title=Report: Mike Golic to stick with ESPN in new role |publisher=Saturdaytradition.com |date= July 13, 2020|accessdate=2022-05-26}}</ref> He also hosted ''[[Golic and Wingo]]'' from 2017 until 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://premierespeakers.com/mike-golic/bio |title=Mike Golic | Bio |publisher=Premiere Speakers Bureau |date=2019-02-06 |accessdate=2022-05-26}}</ref>

After leaving ESPN, in 2021 Golic joined [[Learfield IMG College|Learfield]] as co-host and analyst of College Football Saturday Night, a new personality-driven streaming radio broadcast of college football games throughout the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.learfield.com/2021/09/learfields-new-college-football-saturday-night-with-mike-golic-and-kate-scott-announces-first-three-game-broadcasts/ |title=LEARFIELD's New "College Football Saturday Night" with Mike Golic and Kate Scott Announces First Three Game Broadcasts|publisher=Learfield IMG College|date=September 2, 2021|access-date=October 9, 2021}}</ref> He currently serves as an analyst for [[Profootballtalk.com|Pro Football Talk]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://nbcsportsgrouppressbox.com/2021/09/10/mike-golic-joins-pro-football-talk-with-mike-florio-on-monday-mornings/ |title=Mike Golic Joins Pro Football Talk With Mike Florio On Monday Mornings - Nbc Sports Pressboxnbc Sports Pressbox |publisher=Nbcsportsgrouppressbox.com |date=2021-09-10 |accessdate=2022-05-26}}</ref> and as the analyst for [[NFL on Westwood One Sports|Westwood One]]'s broadcast of Thursday Night Football.

Golic was also the host of the long-running syndicated sports highlights, bloopers, and gag show called ''[[The Lighter Side of Sports]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rotfeldproductions.com/lighterside/ |title=Steve Rotfeld Productions - Lighter Side of Sports |access-date=April 20, 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070927195153/http://www.rotfeldproductions.com/lighterside/ |archive-date=September 27, 2007 }}</ref>

'''Michael John Esposito''' (born April 24, 1953) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player. He is perhaps best known as the player depicted in the logo for the [[East–West Shrine Bowl]].

Esposito attended [[Wilmington High School (Massachusetts)|Wilmington High School]] in Massachusetts<ref>{{cite news|last1=Cooke|first1=Rick|title=After all of these years, Mike Esposito is still a very big deal in Wilmington|url=http://homenewshere.com/wilmington_town_crier/sports/article_71e6e009-dffb-5004-bd4d-9690ffb3bdc1.html|accessdate=January 7, 2015|work=Wilmington Town Crier|date=November 29, 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Pevear|first1=David|title=Ex-Wilmington High football star's invention is on the level|url=http://www.lowellsun.com/football/ci_26267918/ex-wilmington-high-football-stars-invention-is-level|accessdate=January 7, 2015|work=Lowell Sun|date=August 3, 2014}}</ref> and played [[college football]] for the [[Boston College Eagles]] as a [[running back]].<ref>{{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20070208223801/http://www.databasefootball.com/players/playerpage.htm?ilkid=ESPOSMIK01 Mike Esposito Past Stats, Statistics, History, and Awards - databaseFootball.com<!-- Bot generated title -->]}}</ref> He went on to play in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for parts of three seasons (1976–1978) with the [[Atlanta Falcons]].

Esposito was a participant in the 50th edition of the [[East–West Shrine Game]], contested in December 1974 in [[Stanford, California]]. As part of activities leading up to the game, each player would visit the [[Shriners Hospitals for Children]]. While visiting, he noticed Nicole Worley-Urteaga, a two-year-old patient with [[Holt-Oram syndrome]]. She appeared frightened and was crying. Esposito took her hand to calm her down and they walked down the hallway together. A photographer from a local newspaper noticed the scene and snapped a photo of the two. The image became the inspiration for the official logo of the annual all-star contest, now known as the [[East–West Shrine Bowl]], and is displayed annually on the 50-yard line.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://homenewshere.com/wilmington_town_crier/sports/article_71e6e009-dffb-5004-bd4d-9690ffb3bdc1.html|title=After all of these years, Mike Esposito is still a very big deal in Wilmington |first=Rick |last=Cooke |website=homenewshere.com|date=November 29, 2009 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.shrinegame.com/story-behind-the-logo |title=Story Behind the Logo |website=shrinegame.com |accessdate=January 4, 2018}}</ref> Esposito and Urteaga met again prior to the 100th edition of the game, played in January 2025.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://fox40.com/sports/local-sports/the-story-behind-the-shrine-bowl-logo-nicole-urteaga-and-mike-esposito-reunite-for-100th-annual-game/ |title=The story behind the Shrine Bowl logo: Nicole Urteaga and Mike Esposito reunite for 100th annual game |first=Andrew |last=Marden |website=[[KTXL]] |date=February 9, 2025 |accessdate=January 18, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://shrinebowl.com/news/100th-east-west-shrine-bowl-reunites-iconic-pair/ |title=00th East-West Shrine Bowl Reunites Iconic Pair |website=shrinegame.com |access-date=January 18, 2026}}</ref>

'''Michael Kitome Echols''' (born October 13, 1978) is an American former professional [[Gridiron football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] who played in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) and [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). At Wisconsin, he was a four–year starter at cornerback. He finished his career with a recovered [[Fumble (American football)|fumble]] and 12 [[interception]]s, returning one for a touchdown. Before his junior season in 2000, he was suspended one game for receiving unadvertised discounts at a shoe store. After the season, he was given second-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference football teams|All-Big Ten Conference]] honors. In 2002, after graduating from Wisconsin, he declared for the NFL Draft. He was selected by the Titans and debuted later that season. However, after four weeks, he injured his leg and missed the rest of the season. The following season, he saw limited action before being released by the team in 2004. After his stint with the Titans ended, he spent time with the [[Atlanta Falcons]], [[Indianapolis Colts]], and [[Detroit Lions]], failing to appear in a game for any of the teams. In 2006, Echols played his final professional game for the [[Hamilton Tiger-Cats]] of the CFL, intercepting a pass in his only game for the team.
